findings.description: Homogeneous mode toggle Pressable has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityHint.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="radio" accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.demand.homogeneous')} accessibilityState={{ checked: fallbackMode === 'homogeneous' }} accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.demand.homogeneousHint')}

findings.description: Manual counts mode toggle Pressable has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityHint.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="radio" accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.demand.manualCounts')} accessibilityState={{ checked: fallbackMode === 'manual' }} accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.demand.manualCountsHint')}

findings.description: Save Baseline Pressable is missing accessibilityRole and accessibilityHint.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.demand.saveBaseline')} accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.demand.saveBaselineHint')}

findings.description: Save Target Pressable is missing accessibilityRole and accessibilityHint.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.demand.saveTarget')} accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.demand.saveTargetHint')}

findings.description: Forecast action Pressable is missing accessibilityRole, accessibilityHint, and does not expose disabled state via accessibilityState.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityState={{ disabled: forecastActionDisabled }} accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.demand.runForecastHint')} and use the disabled prop instead of guarding inside onPress.

findings.description: Inline error and success messages are not announced to screen readers when they appear.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap error/success ThemedText in a View with accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" (or 'assertive' for errors) so VoiceOver/TalkBack announces the message automatically.

findings.description: demandTargets list items have no accessibilityRole, making the list structure invisible to screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="listitem" to each row View and wrap the entire map output in a View with accessibilityRole="list".

findings.description: No returnKeyType or onSubmitEditing chaining between the role and startDate InputFields.
findings.proposed_fix: Add returnKeyType="next" and onSubmitEditing to focus the next field; add returnKeyType="done" to the last field in the form.

findings.description: Toggle chip Pressables are not reachable via Tab key on web because Pressable does not render a focusable element without tabIndex.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tabIndex={0} (or use a button element on web via role prop) and ensure onKeyDown handles Enter/Space to trigger the mode change.

findings.description: No autoFocus on the first InputField of the fallback form, so keyboard users have no automatic entry point.
findings.proposed_fix: Add autoFocus to the first InputField (role) so focus lands there when the section mounts.

findings.description: Save Baseline uses styles.secondaryButton + styles.tightButton while Save Target uses only styles.primaryButton, yet both have identical primaryButtonText styles — visually inconsistent sibling submit actions.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide on a single button variant for all submit actions and apply it consistently; if visual distinction is intentional, document it and ensure text colour contracts match each variant.

findings.description: Forecast Pressable is disabled by conditionally guarding runForecast inside onPress rather than using the disabled prop, so the button lacks native disabled styling cues beyond styles.disabledButton.
findings.proposed_fix: Use disabled={forecastActionDisabled} prop on Pressable and move runForecast directly to onPress; rely on styles.disabledButton for visual state.

findings.description: When demandTargets is an empty array the list renders nothing with no empty-state message or CTA to guide the user.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a conditional: if demandTargets.length === 0, render a ThemedText empty-state message such as t('scheduler.demand.noTargets') plus a CTA linking to the add-target form.

findings.description: Inline arrow functions passed to both toggle Pressables create new function references on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize handlers with useCallback: const setHomogeneous = useCallback(() => setFallbackMode('homogeneous'), [setFallbackMode]); const setManual = useCallback(() => setFallbackMode('manual'), [setFallbackMode]);

findings.description: Inline arrow function wrapping runForecast with a guard creates a new function reference every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with disabled={forecastActionDisabled} and onPress={runForecast} directly, eliminating the wrapper entirely.

findings.description: demandTargets.map is called unconditionally in render with a template-literal key computation on every render cycle.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure the parent memoises demandTargets (useMemo/selector) so the map only re-runs when the array reference changes; the key pattern itself is acceptable.

findings.description: baselineTargetsRef.current ?? demandTargets creates a new expression value on every render, potentially causing unnecessary LostRevenueSummary re-renders.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute const baselineTargets = baselineTargetsRef.current ?? demandTargets outside JSX with useMemo, or lift the fallback resolution to the parent.

findings.description: The bullet separator ' • ' between CI range and confidence percentage is a hardcoded English/punctuation string.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the separator inside the translation string: t('scheduler.demand.confidenceSeparator', { pct: ... }) so locales can customise or omit it.

findings.description: The fallback string 'model' for target.source is a hardcoded English literal.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with target.source ?? t('scheduler.demand.sourceDefault') so the fallback is translatable.

findings.description: The 'Save Shift' Pressable is missing accessibilityRole='button', leaving screen readers without semantic context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" to the Pressable element.

findings.description: The 'Auto-Assign' Pressable is missing accessibilityRole='button', leaving screen readers without semantic context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" to the Pressable element.

findings.description: The 'Apply Auto-Assign' Pressable is missing accessibilityRole='button' and accessibilityHint, and does not communicate its disabled state via accessibilityState.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button", an accessibilityHint, and accessibilityState={{ disabled: autoAssignApplying }} to the Pressable.

findings.description: templateError is rendered as plain ThemedText with no accessibilityRole='alert', so screen readers will not announce it automatically when it appears.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap or replace with <ThemedText accessibilityRole="alert" accessibilityLiveRegion="assertive" style={styles.errorText}>{templateError}</ThemedText>.

findings.description: shiftError is rendered as plain ThemedText with no accessibilityRole='alert', so screen readers will not announce it automatically when it appears.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="alert" and accessibilityLiveRegion="assertive" to the ThemedText rendering shiftError.

findings.description: templateSuccessMessage is rendered as plain ThemedText with no live region, so screen readers will not announce success to the user.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="status" and accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" to the success message ThemedText.

findings.description: WorkerId and templateId InputFields in the shifts section are missing accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint, unlike their counterparts in the template form.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.shifts.workerA11y')} and accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.shifts.workerA11yHint')} to all three shift InputFields.

findings.description: No returnKeyType or onSubmitEditing is set on any InputField in the template form, so keyboard users cannot tab through or submit the form with the return key.
findings.proposed_fix: Chain fields using refs: set returnKeyType="next" and onSubmitEditing to focus the next InputField; set returnKeyType="done" on the last field (coverage) and trigger handleAddTemplate.

findings.description: No returnKeyType or onSubmitEditing is set on any InputField in the shift form, preventing keyboard-only form submission.
findings.proposed_fix: Set returnKeyType="next" on workerId and templateId fields with onSubmitEditing chaining; set returnKeyType="done" on date field and trigger handleShiftSubmit.

findings.description: No autoFocus on the first InputField of the 'Add Template' form, so keyboard users opening this card must manually navigate to the first field.
findings.proposed_fix: Add autoFocus prop to the first InputField (template name) so focus lands there when the card is rendered.

findings.description: The 'Save Shift' button uses styles.primaryButton but its sibling 'Auto-Assign' uses styles.secondaryButton, yet both apply styles.primaryButtonText, creating inconsistent text colour semantics.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply styles.secondaryButtonText to the secondary button's ThemedText, or unify the text style tokens so primary/secondary distinction is visually clear.

findings.description: The 'Apply' Pressable conditionally applies styles.disabledButton but has no cursor or opacity change communicated to web users since accessibilityState.disabled is absent.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityState={{ disabled: autoAssignApplying }} and ensure styles.disabledButton includes opacity: 0.5 and cursor: 'not-allowed' for web parity.

findings.description: The auto-assign suggestions block renders nothing (null) when autoAssignSuggestions is an empty array, with no feedback to the user that auto-assign ran but found no valid assignments.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an else branch: when autoAssignSuggestions is a non-null empty array, render a ThemedText explaining no suggestions were found, e.g. t('scheduler.shifts.noSuggestions').

findings.description: Inside the autoAssignSuggestions map, workers.find() and shiftTemplates.find() are called per suggestion on every render, making lookups O(n*m) with no memoisation.
findings.current_value: const workerName = workers.find((w) => w.id === s.workerId)?.name ?? s.workerId;
findings.proposed_fix: Derive workerMap and templateMap with useMemo outside the render: const workerMap = useMemo(() => Object.fromEntries(workers.map(w => [w.id, w.name])), [workers]); and use workerMap[s.workerId] inside the map.

findings.description: updateTemplateField('name') and similar calls create a new function reference on every render because the curried call happens inline in JSX.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize each handler with useMemo or useCallback outside JSX, e.g. const onChangeName = useCallback(updateTemplateField('name'), [updateTemplateField]), and pass onChangeName as the prop.

findings.description: The ghost preview map over [0, 1] creates a new array literal on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist const GHOST_INDICES = [0, 1] outside the component so the array reference is stable across renders.

findings.description: Placeholder strings '09:00' and '17:00' for start and end time fields are hardcoded English/locale-specific values not routed through t().
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with placeholder={t('scheduler.templates.startPlaceholder')} and placeholder={t('scheduler.templates.endPlaceholder')} to allow locale-aware time format hints.

findings.description: The ghost preview container uses accessibilityElementsHidden but is not also wrapped with importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants' for Android screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" alongside accessibilityElementsHidden to ensure the ghost is hidden on both iOS and Android.

findings.description: Publish Pressable has a static accessibilityLabel that does not include the shift identity, making it indistinguishable from sibling publish buttons for screen-reader users.
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.roster.publishA11y', { worker: shift.worker?.name ?? shift.workerId, date })} — e.g. 'Publish shift for Alice on 2025-06-10'

findings.description: Unpublish Pressable has a static accessibilityLabel that does not identify which shift is being unpublished.
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.roster.unpublishA11y', { worker: shift.worker?.name ?? shift.workerId, date })} — e.g. 'Unpublish shift for Alice on 2025-06-10'

findings.description: Notify Pressable has a static accessibilityLabel that does not identify which shift or worker is being notified.
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.roster.notifyA11y', { worker: shift.worker?.name ?? shift.workerId, date })} — e.g. 'Notify Alice about shift on 2025-06-10'

findings.description: All three Pressables are missing accessibilityHint, leaving screen-reader users without context about the action's effect.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityHint to each: e.g. publish → 'Makes this shift visible to the assigned worker'; unpublish → 'Reverts shift to draft and hides it from the worker'; notify → 'Sends a push notification to the assigned worker'

findings.description: Disabled Pressables do not set accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }}, so assistive technologies cannot announce them as disabled.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityState={{ disabled: shift.status === 'Published' }} (and equivalents) to each Pressable alongside the disabled prop.

findings.description: The date heading inside each rosterDay group has no accessibilityRole, so screen readers do not convey it as a section header.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="header" to the date ThemedText, or wrap in a View with accessibilityRole="header".

findings.description: The 'Secured' badge View has no accessibilityLabel or accessibilityRole, so its meaning is lost to screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="status" and accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.roster.secured')} to the badge View, and optionally accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" so it is announced when it appears.

findings.description: The Unpublish and Notify chips omit styles.actionChipPrimary / variant style that the Publish chip has, creating visually inconsistent siblings.
findings.proposed_fix: Define distinct variant StyleSheet entries (actionChipPrimary, actionChipSecondary, actionChipDestructive) and apply consistently to all three chips, or explicitly apply actionChipSecondary to unpublish and notify chips.

findings.description: Disabled visual state relies solely on styles.disabledButton with no opacity or color change visible in the style definition; there is no accessible colour-contrast fallback.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure styles.disabledButton sets opacity: 0.4 (or equivalent reduced contrast) and verify it meets WCAG 1.4.3 for disabled text; add accessibilityState={{ disabled }} as noted in RS-005.

findings.description: Object.entries(rosterByDate) is called twice in render — once for the empty check and once for mapping — causing two full object traversals every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive const rosterEntries = Object.entries(rosterByDate); outside JSX (useMemo if rosterByDate identity changes often) and reference rosterEntries in both places.

findings.description: Inline arrow functions are created on every render for all three onPress handlers inside the shifts.map loop, bypassing stable reference optimisation.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap each row in a memoised RosterRow sub-component that receives the id and the stable handler, or use useCallback with shift.id in a dedicated row component.

findings.description: Inline array literal [0, 1] is created as a new object on every render inside the ghost-skeleton map.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist const GHOST_ROWS = [0, 1]; to module scope so the array is allocated once.

findings.description: Inline style object literal { width: 52 } is allocated on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ghostBadgeBarWide: { width: 52 } to the StyleSheet and reference styles.ghostBadgeBarWide.

findings.description: When rosterByDate is empty the ghost skeleton renders decorative placeholder rows but there is no actionable CTA (e.g. a button to create a first shift), only descriptive text.
findings.proposed_fix: Render a Pressable/Button CTA below the empty description that navigates to shift-creation, with accessibilityRole="button" and a label such as t('scheduler.roster.createFirstShift').

findings.description: The date string rendered as a section header is passed through directly from a Record key without locale-aware date formatting.
findings.proposed_fix: Format via Intl.DateTimeFormat or a shared formatDate(date, locale) utility so the date respects the active locale's conventions before rendering.

findings.description: shift.date in the upcoming-shifts section is rendered raw without locale-aware formatting.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply the same formatDate(shift.date, locale) utility used elsewhere to ensure consistent, locale-aware date display.

findings.description: SignOutButton Pressable has no accessibilityHint, leaving screen-reader users without context about what signing out will do.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityHint="Ends your session and returns you to the sign-in screen" to the Pressable.

findings.description: The SignOutButton renders only an icon inside the Pressable; if the icon fails to render, there is no visible or accessible text fallback for the button label.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an <AccessibilityInfo>-safe visually-hidden label or wrap with an accessible Text node: <Text style={styles.srOnly}>Sign out</Text> alongside the icon.

findings.description: Tab bar icons (house.fill, calendar, chart.bar.fill) have no accessibilityLabel; relying solely on the tab title means the icon Pressable area has no programmatic label on its own.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass accessibilityLabel matching the tab title to each IconSymbol, e.g. accessibilityLabel={t('nav.home')} on the icon, or ensure HapticTab forwards the screen title as the accessible label.

findings.description: The headerRight View wrapping LanguageSelector and extraHeaderRight has no accessibilityRole or label, so grouped interactive controls lack a landmark for screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="toolbar" and accessibilityLabel="Header actions" to the wrapping View.

findings.description: SignOutButton uses an inline style object literal instead of a StyleSheet entry, inconsistent with any StyleSheet-based styles elsewhere and causing a new object on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to StyleSheet.create({ signOutButton: { paddingHorizontal: 14, paddingVertical: 8 } }) and reference as style={styles.signOutButton}.

findings.description: SignOutButton has no disabled state styling or disabled prop; if signOut is in-flight the button remains fully interactive with no visual feedback.
findings.proposed_fix: Track a loading state: const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false); set disabled={loading} and apply reduced opacity style when loading is true.

findings.description: headerRightContent is a JSX element created as a plain variable inside the render body of TabNavigator; it is recreated on every render, causing React to remount the header subtree.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize with useMemo: const headerRightContent = useMemo(() => (<View ...>...</View>), [langCode, setLanguage, locale, extraHeaderRight, colorScheme]);

findings.description: headerRight is an inline arrow function () => headerRightContent passed to screenOptions, creating a new function reference on every render and triggering unnecessary header re-renders.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap with useCallback: const renderHeaderRight = useCallback(() => headerRightContent, [headerRightContent]); then headerRight: renderHeaderRight.

findings.description: onPress={() => signOut()} is a new inline function created on every render of SignOutButton.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with onPress={signOut} directly, or useCallback: const handleSignOut = useCallback(() => signOut(), [signOut]);

findings.description: The accessibilityLabel "Sign out" is a hardcoded English string not passed through the t() localisation function.
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityLabel={t('auth.signOut')}

findings.description: The inline style object on the header-right View is a new object literal created every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to StyleSheet.create({ headerRight: { flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, paddingRight: 12 } }).

findings.description: The 'explore' tab screen title uses t('nav.analytics') but the screen name is 'explore', creating a mismatch that could confuse assistive technology users navigating by tab name.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the screen to 'analytics' or align the translation key to t('nav.explore') to ensure the route name and announced label are consistent.

findings.description: The section heading 'Achievements' has no accessibilityRole, so screen readers cannot identify it as a heading.
findings.proposed_fix: <ThemedText type="subtitle" accessibilityRole="header">Achievements</ThemedText>

findings.description: Each achievement card View has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, so screen readers announce it as an unlabelled group with no context.
findings.proposed_fix: <ThemedView key={achievement.id} style={styles.card} accessibilityRole="group" accessibilityLabel={`${achievement.title}: ${percent}% complete, ${achievement.progress} of ${safeGoal}`}>

findings.description: The progress bar track View exposes no accessibility semantics; screen readers skip or misread the visual progress indicator.
findings.proposed_fix:
<View style={styles.progressTrack} accessibilityRole="progressbar" accessibilityValue={{ min: 0, max: safeGoal, now: achievement.progress }} accessibilityLabel={`Progress: ${percent}%`}>
  <View style={[styles.progressFill, { width: `${percent}%` }]} />
</View>

findings.description: The '{progress} of {safeGoal}' text duplicates information already in the progress bar but is also the only human-readable count; there is no accessibilityLabel tying it to the parent achievement.
findings.proposed_fix:
<ThemedText style={styles.helperText} accessibilityLabel={`${achievement.progress} of ${safeGoal} completed`} importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants">
  {achievement.progress} of {safeGoal}
</ThemedText>

findings.description: When items is empty the component renders nothing (null), giving users no feedback that achievements exist but none have been earned yet.
The section title 'Achievements' is a hardcoded English string not wrapped in a translation call.
findings.proposed_fix: {t('profile.achievements.title')}

findings.description: The '{progress} of {safeGoal}' progress label is a hardcoded English string with no i18n wrapper.
findings.proposed_fix: {t('profile.achievements.progressLabel', { progress: achievement.progress, goal: safeGoal })}

findings.description: A new inline style object literal `{ width: \`${percent}%\` }` is created on every render for every card, bypassing StyleSheet memoisation.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the style outside JSX: `const fillStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.progressFill, { width: `${percent}%` as DimensionValue }], [percent]);` then use `style={fillStyle}`; or derive it per-item before the return.

findings.description: The entire items.map() with per-item arithmetic (Math.min, Math.max, Math.round) runs unconditionally on every render with no memoisation.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the mapped list in useMemo: `const renderedItems = useMemo(() => items.map(...), [items]);` and render `{renderedItems}`.

findings.description: The card background is hardcoded '#ffffff' while the container uses a transparent tint '#ffffff11', breaking dark-mode theming consistency; ThemedView's theme token should drive the background.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the hardcoded backgroundColor from the card style and rely on ThemedView's themed background, or pass a themed colour from useThemeColor().

findings.description: The progress fill colour '#2563EB' is hardcoded and will not adapt to theme or user-defined accent colour.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a design-token value sourced from useThemeColor() or a shared theme constant, e.g. Colors.light.tint.

findings.description: The badge value '{percent}%' uses a hardcoded percent sign which may not format correctly for all locales.
findings.proposed_fix: {new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(achievement.progress / safeGoal)}

findings.description: The 'emptyStateCta' Pressable inside the upcoming-shifts empty state is missing an accessibilityHint, leaving screen-reader users without context on what navigating there accomplishes.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityHint={t('home.upcomingShifts.buildFirstHint')} alongside the existing label, e.g. 'Opens the scheduler so you can create your first shift'.

findings.description: The hero logo-mark View ('H' monogram) has no accessibilityLabel or accessibilityRole, so VoiceOver/TalkBack announces it as an unlabelled element.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="image" accessibilityLabel="Horario logo" to the outer heroLogoMark View, and set importantForAccessibility="no" on the inner ThemedText to avoid double-reading.

findings.description: Each staffing-gap row exposes raw gap/required counts without a combined accessible label, so TalkBack reads three disconnected fragments instead of a meaningful summary.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap each gap row View with accessibilityRole="listitem" and accessibilityLabel={`${gap.role}, ${gap.date}, ${gap.gap} open of ${gap.required} required`} so the entire row is read as one unit.

findings.description: Each upcoming-shift row View has no accessibilityRole or combined label, causing assistive technology to read worker name, template, and date as separate unrelated elements.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="listitem" and accessibilityLabel={`${shift.workerName}, ${shift.templateName}, ${shift.templateStart}–${shift.templateEnd}, ${shift.date}`} to the row View.

findings.description: The ProfileAchievements items array is constructed with a new object literal on every render, causing unnecessary child re-renders even when streakCount has not changed.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the array: const achievements = useMemo(() => [{ id: 'ach-1', ..., progress: Math.max(streakCount, 1) }, { id: 'ach-2', ... }], [streakCount, t]); then pass items={achievements}.

findings.description: An inline arrow function is passed as the onSelectItem prop on every render, breaking referential equality and preventing PersonalizedFeed from bailing out with React.memo.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract with useCallback: const handleFeedSelect = useCallback((item) => { if (item.category === 'availability') recordAction(); }, [recordAction]); then pass onSelectItem={handleFeedSelect}.

findings.description: usePersonalizedFeed is called with a new options object literal on every render, which may cause the hook to re-run unnecessarily if it uses the object as a dependency.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist the options object outside the component: const FEED_OPTIONS = { focus: 'availability', prefersShortTasks: true } and pass that constant, or memoize inside the hook with JSON-stable comparison.

findings.description: The three quick-action Pressables use actionButton style (borderRadius: 10, padding: 12) while the primary CTA uses borderRadius: 10 with asymmetric paddingVertical/paddingHorizontal, and the emptyStateCta Pressable has no padding or borderRadius at all, breaking visual consistency across siblings.
findings.current_value: primaryButton: { paddingVertical: 10, paddingHorizontal: 16, borderRadius: 10 } vs emptyStateCta: { marginTop: 6, alignSelf: 'flex-start' }
findings.proposed_fix: Define a shared base button token (padding: 12, borderRadius: 10) in StyleSheet and compose variants from it; ensure emptyStateCta has at minimum paddingVertical: 8, paddingHorizontal: 12, borderRadius: 10.

findings.description: No Pressable in the file handles a disabled visual state; if the parent hook is loading (rosterLoading), interactive buttons remain fully styled and clickable without opacity or color feedback.
findings.current_value: style={styles.primaryButton} — no disabled prop or style variant
findings.proposed_fix: Use the style callback form: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.primaryButton, pressed && styles.pressed, isDisabled && styles.disabledButton]} and define disabledButton: { opacity: 0.4 } in StyleSheet.

findings.description: PersonalizedFeed is rendered unconditionally with whatever feedItems the hook returns; if the hook yields an empty array there is no empty-state message or CTA visible to the user.
findings.proposed_fix: Guard the card: {feedItems.length === 0 ? <ThemedText style={styles.mutedText}>{t('home.feed.empty')}</ThemedText> : <PersonalizedFeed items={feedItems} ... />} or handle it inside PersonalizedFeed with an emptyState prop.

findings.description: The heroTagline text 'Smart scheduling, simplified.' is a hardcoded English string not wrapped in a t() call.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with <ThemedText style={styles.heroTagline}>{t('home.hero.heroTagline')}</ThemedText> and add the key to all locale files.

findings.description: The heroWordmark text 'Horario' is hardcoded English (product name) without a t() call; while a brand name may intentionally stay untranslated, the aria-accessible heroContainer has no locale-aware label.
findings.proposed_fix: If the brand name is intentionally untranslated, add accessibilityLabel={t('home.hero.logoAlt')} to the heroContainer View so localised screen-reader text remains possible.

findings.description: On Expo web, Pressable does not automatically receive a keyboard-focusable role; the primary CTA wrapped in Link should also include tabIndex={0} and an onKeyDown Enter handler to be reachable via Tab key.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tabIndex={0} and onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === 'Enter' && e.currentTarget.click()} to all Pressable elements that are wrapped in Link asChild on web targets.

findings.description: The StreakCounter rewardMessage prop is sourced from tier.message which may be an unchecked long string exceeding 120 characters, risking verbose tooltip copy.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce a max length in useEthicalReward: ensure tier.message is ≤ 80 characters, or truncate in the StreakCounter component with a numberOfLines={2} cap.

findings.description: The upcoming-shifts and staffing-gaps lists have no wrapping accessibilityRole='list' container, so screen readers cannot announce the item count or navigate by list shortcuts.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap each .map() result in a View with accessibilityRole="list" so TalkBack/VoiceOver announces 'list, N items' before reading children.

findings.description: Pressable for opening forecast setup has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityHint, making it invisible to screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.missingData.openSetup')} accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.missingData.openSetupHint')} to the Pressable.

findings.description: The actionBanner ThemedView conveys dynamic success/error status but has no accessibilityRole='alert' or accessibilityLiveRegion, so screen readers won't announce changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="alert" accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" (or 'assertive' for errors) to the actionBanner ThemedView.

findings.description: The needsFallbackSetup warning banner has no accessibilityRole or live-region annotation, so urgent missing-data warnings are not surfaced to assistive technologies.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="alert" accessibilityLiveRegion="assertive" to this ThemedView.

findings.description: The link-styled ThemedText child of the Pressable reads as plain text to screen readers with no role indication that it is interactive.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the nested ThemedText and instead render the label directly via accessibilityLabel on the Pressable, or ensure the Pressable has accessibilityRole="link" so assistive tech announces it correctly.

findings.description: The Pressable inside the warning banner is not reachable via Tab key on web because Pressable does not receive keyboard focus by default in React Native Web without explicit focusable or tabIndex props.
findings.proposed_fix: Add focusable={true} and onKeyDown handler (Enter/Space) or replace with a web-accessible TouchableOpacity / custom button that sets tabIndex={0} on web.

findings.description: WorkerSection receives workers which may be an empty array on first load, but there is no guard or empty-state message passed at the orchestration level to confirm a fallback is handled inside WorkerSection.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify WorkerSection renders an empty-state CTA when workers.length === 0; if not, pass an emptyStateLabel prop such as t('scheduler.workers.empty') with a prompt to add the first worker.

findings.description: ShiftTemplateSection receives shiftTemplates which may be empty, but no empty-state message or CTA is passed at the orchestration layer.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass an emptyStateLabel such as t('scheduler.templates.empty') or confirm the sub-component handles this; add a visible CTA guiding the user to create their first template.

findings.description: RosterSection receives upcomingShifts and staffingGaps which may both be empty arrays with no empty-state UI surfaced at this layer.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure RosterSection renders a meaningful empty state such as t('scheduler.roster.noShifts') with a CTA to create or assign shifts when upcomingShifts is empty.

findings.description: Inline arrow function passed to onPress creates a new function reference on every render, preventing referential stability.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to a useCallback: const handleOpenForecastSetup = useCallback(() => router.setParams({ section: 'forecast' }), [router]); and pass handleOpenForecastSetup.

findings.description: Array literal with conditional values is constructed inline in the style prop on every render, creating a new array reference each time.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive bannerStyle with useMemo: const bannerStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.banner, actionBanner?.type === 'success' && styles.bannerSuccess, actionBanner?.type === 'error' && styles.bannerError], [actionBanner?.type]);

findings.description: Inline arrow function passed to onLayout for workerSectionRef creates a new function on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to useCallback: const handleWorkerSectionLayout = useCallback((e) => setWorkerSectionOffset(e.nativeEvent.layout.y), [setWorkerSectionOffset]);

findings.description: Inline onLayout arrow functions on templateSectionRef, shiftSectionRef, and demandSectionRef also recreate on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Create stable useCallback equivalents for each layout setter, mirroring the fix for SCH-011.

findings.description: The comment string '── shiftSectionRef anchors scroll-to-shift-section' is developer-only but any visible text labels inside sub-components should be audited; no hardcoded strings detected at this layer.
findings.proposed_fix: No action needed for the comment itself; confirm all string props passed to sub-components (e.g. fallbackMessage, workerSuccessMessage) originate from t() calls inside the hook.

findings.description: The Pressable in the warning banner has no disabled state handling and no visual pressed/focused feedback style defined at this layer, inconsistent with other interactive elements in the screen.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a style callback: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.linkButton, pressed && styles.linkButtonPressed]} and ensure a focused style via android_ripple or web :focus-visible equivalent for consistency.

findings.description: ScrollView has an accessibilityLabel intended for landmark identification but ScrollView is not a landmark element; this label will be read as the container name, which is confusing on screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove accessibilityLabel from ScrollView and instead wrap the header ThemedView with accessibilityRole='header'. If a region label is needed, use a wrapping View with accessibilityRole='none' or add a visually-hidden heading.

findings.description: MetricCard is a purely presentational card but contains no accessibilityRole and no accessible grouping, so screen readers read out value and label as disconnected strings.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole='text' (or 'summary') and accessibilityLabel={`${label}: ${value}${sub ? ', ' + sub : ''}`} to the outer ThemedView of MetricCard so the whole card is announced as one unit.

findings.description: HoursBar row has no accessibilityLabel; screen readers will announce the raw worker name, bar (invisible View), and hours as three separate unrelated elements.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole='none' importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants' to inner Views, and on the outer View: accessibilityLabel={`${name}: ${hours.toFixed(1)} hours`}.

findings.description: FairnessGauge has no accessibilityLabel; the color-coded bar is invisible to screen readers and the label + score are read as separate fragments.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityLabel={`${label}, fairness standard deviation ${score.toFixed(1)}`} and accessibilityRole='none' on the outer View, marking inner decorative Views with importantForAccessibility='no'.

findings.description: The revenue card's ThemedText displaying the revenue value has a dynamic color (red/green) as the only signal for positive/negative state; color alone is not sufficient for accessibility.
findings.proposed_fix: Supplement color with an accessibilityLabel on the ThemedText, e.g. accessibilityLabel={`${formatCurrency(uncoveredRevenue)}, ${uncoveredRevenue > 0 ? t('analytics.atRisk') : t('analytics.allCovered')}`}.

findings.description: The 'openScheduler' translation key is used for both the accessibilityLabel and the visible button text, making the hint redundant and providing no extra context beyond the label.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the visible text as-is. Change accessibilityLabel to a slightly more descriptive string, e.g. t('analytics.openSchedulerA11y') = 'Open shift scheduler' and ensure accessibilityHint describes the navigation destination.

findings.description: The retry Pressable and the primary action Pressable are not reachable via Tab key on Expo web because they lack focusable/tabIndex props.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tabIndex={0} and onKeyDown handler (or use a <button> via react-native-web's accessible prop) so keyboard users can activate both Pressables on web: tabIndex={0} accessible={true}.

findings.description: accessibilityHint for retry button depends entirely on t('analytics.retryA11yHint') whose key name suggests it may be a long sentence; hints should be ≤120 chars and action-oriented.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure the translation value is ≤80 chars, e.g. 'Reloads analytics data from the server'.

findings.description: retryButton and primaryButton share identical padding (10/20 vs 10) and borderRadius (10) but primaryButton omits paddingHorizontal, producing visually inconsistent siblings.
findings.current_value: retryButton: { paddingVertical:10, paddingHorizontal:20, borderRadius:10 } vs primaryButton: { paddingVertical:10, borderRadius:10 }
findings.proposed_fix: Standardise to a shared base style: paddingVertical:12, paddingHorizontal:24, borderRadius:10. Extract a shared actionButton style in StyleSheet and spread it in both.

findings.description: Neither retryButton nor primaryButton visually communicates a disabled state; if the parent logic ever disables them, there is no opacity or color change.
findings.current_value: No disabled style or disabled prop handling present
findings.proposed_fix: Add a disabled prop to both Pressables and use style={({ pressed, disabled }) => [styles.primaryButton, disabled && styles.buttonDisabled]} with buttonDisabled: { opacity: 0.5 }.

findings.description: The Quick Actions card only ever shows a single Link/Pressable; if the actions list were data-driven and empty, there is no empty-state guard.
findings.current_value: <ThemedView style={styles.card}> with a single hardcoded Pressable
findings.proposed_fix: If actions become data-driven, add an empty-state: {actions.length === 0 && <ThemedText>{t('analytics.noActions')}</ThemedText>}.

findings.description: Inline object literal `{ borderLeftColor: accent, borderLeftWidth: 3 }` is created on every render inside MetricCard, causing unnecessary style reconciliation.
findings.current_value: style={[styles.metricCard, accent ? { borderLeftColor: accent, borderLeftWidth: 3 } : null]}
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the accent style with useMemo inside MetricCard: const accentStyle = useMemo(() => accent ? { borderLeftColor: accent, borderLeftWidth: 3 } : null, [accent]);

findings.description: The accent color for the coverage MetricCard is computed via a ternary chain directly in JSX, creating a new expression on every render of AnalyticsScreen.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to a useMemo or a pure helper: const coverageAccent = useMemo(() => coverageRate >= 80 ? '#15803D' : coverageRate >= 50 ? '#B45309' : '#DC2626', [coverageRate]);

findings.description: `.map()` over workerHours inside JSX with a cast `(workerHours as WorkerHoursEntry[])` runs on every render with no memoization.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap in useMemo: const hoursBars = useMemo(() => workerHours.map(entry => <HoursBar key={entry.workerId} ... />), [workerHours, maxHours]); then render {hoursBars}.

findings.description: The hours unit suffix 'h' in HoursBar is hardcoded English and not wrapped in a translation call.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with {t('common.hoursShort', { n: hours.toFixed(1) })} where the translation value is e.g. '{{n}}h' (or localised equivalent).

findings.description: The HoursBar accessible label (proposed fix EXP-003) would hardcode the 'hours' word; the template must also be i18n-wrapped.
findings.proposed_fix: Use t('analytics.workerHoursA11y', { name, hours: hours.toFixed(1) }) for the accessibilityLabel string.

findings.description: The 'Close tooltip' full-screen dismiss Pressable is missing accessibilityRole and accessibilityHint, making its purpose ambiguous to screen-reader users.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" and accessibilityHint="Dismisses the help tooltip" to the full-screen Pressable.

findings.description: The native 'Close' button has an accessibilityLabel of 'Close' which is vague and does not describe what is being closed.
findings.proposed_fix: Change to accessibilityLabel="Close help tooltip" and add accessibilityHint="Dismisses the help information card".

findings.description: The web tooltip card View is not exposed to assistive technology — it has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or aria-modal, so screen readers cannot identify or navigate it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="tooltip", accessibilityLabel={label} (or a derivative), and aria-modal where supported, so assistive tech announces the tooltip card.

findings.description: The native modal overlay View containing the tooltip card has no accessibilityViewIsModal or accessibilityRole, so focus is not trapped inside the modal for screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityViewIsModal={true} and accessibilityRole="alert" (or 'dialog' on web) to the nativeOverlay View.

findings.description: On web, the Modal does not trap keyboard focus inside the tooltip card; Tab key can reach elements behind the transparent backdrop, breaking keyboard UX.
findings.proposed_fix: On web, render a focus-trap wrapper (e.g. react-focus-lock or a manual tabIndex/-1 sentinel approach) around the tooltip card when visible, and restore focus to buttonRef on close.

findings.description: The ⓘ button does not handle onKeyDown for Enter/Space on web, so keyboard-only users who tab to it cannot trigger it via standard key conventions.
findings.proposed_fix: On web add onKeyDown handler: if event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ' ' call measureAndShow() and event.preventDefault().

findings.description: When the tooltip card appears on web it does not receive programmatic focus, so keyboard users must Tab blindly to reach its content.
findings.proposed_fix: After setVisible(true), use a ref on the tooltip card and call .focus() (with tabIndex={-1} on the card View) so focus moves into the tooltip.

findings.description: The accessibilityHint for web ('Shows help information for this section') is generic and not specific to what the tooltip contains.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the hint from the content prop, e.g. `Tap to show: ${content.slice(0, 60)}${content.length > 60 ? '…' : ''}` or accept a dedicated hintText prop.

findings.description: The accessibilityHint for native says 'Long press for help information' but the button also responds to a normal tap, making the hint misleading.
findings.proposed_fix: Change to 'Tap or long press to show help information'.

findings.description: The native 'Got it ✓' close button uses a StyleSheet-defined style but has no pressed/disabled visual state, unlike the ⓘ button which has iconButtonPressed.
findings.proposed_fix: Convert to a style callback: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.closeButton, pressed && styles.closeButtonPressed]} and define closeButtonPressed with reduced opacity or darkened background.

findings.description: The closeButton has borderRadius: 8 while the iconButton has borderRadius: 12; sibling interactive elements should use a consistent border-radius token.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a shared BORDER_RADIUS constant (e.g. 8) and apply it to both buttons, or document intentional differing radii with a comment.

findings.description: The hardcoded string 'Got it ✓' inside the close button is not wrapped in a translation call.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with {t('tooltip.close')} (or equivalent i18n call) and add the key to translation files.

findings.description: The default label prop value 'More information' and both accessibilityHint strings are hardcoded English and not passed through an i18n function.
findings.current_value: label = 'More information', 'Shows help information for this section', 'Long press for help information'
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap each string with t(): label = t('tooltip.label'), hints via t('tooltip.hintWeb') and t('tooltip.hintNative').

findings.description: estimateCardHeight() is called inside measureAndShow (which is a useCallback) on every invocation but its inputs (content, tooltipW, maxCardH) are stable between renders; memoising the result would avoid redundant computation on rapid hover events.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist to useMemo: const approxH = useMemo(() => estimateCardHeight(content, tooltipW, maxCardH), [content, tooltipW, maxCardH]) and reference it inside measureAndShow.

findings.description: An inline style object array is constructed on every render for the positioned tooltip card, creating new object references each time.
findings.current_value: style={[styles.tooltipCard, { position: 'absolute', top: cardPos.y, left: cardPos.x, width: tooltipW, maxHeight: maxCardH }]}
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the position style with useMemo keyed on cardPos, tooltipW and maxCardH, then spread into the array.

findings.description: An inline style object for the native card is also recreated on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize with useMemo: const nativeCardStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.tooltipCard, { width: tooltipW, maxHeight: maxCardH }], [tooltipW, maxCardH]).

findings.description: Pressable log button is missing accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, and accessibilityHint, making it unidentifiable to screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button", accessibilityLabel={isFresh ? 'Already logged for today' : 'Log today\'s progress'}, accessibilityHint={isFresh ? '' : 'Records your activity and extends your streak'}, and accessibilityState={{ disabled: isFresh }}.

findings.description: Disabled state of the log button is communicated only via opacity and the disabled prop but not via accessibilityState, so screen readers won't announce it as disabled.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityState={{ disabled: isFresh }} to the Pressable alongside the existing disabled prop.

findings.description: The badge displaying the streak count has no accessibilityLabel, so screen readers will read raw numbers without context.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the badge ThemedView with accessibilityRole="text" and accessibilityLabel={`Current streak: ${streakCount} days`}.

findings.description: The rewardCard ThemedView has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, leaving reward information unannounced in a structured way for screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="alert" (or "region") and accessibilityLabel={`Reward unlocked: ${rewardTitle}`} so screen readers announce it when it appears.

findings.description: The Pressable is not focusable via keyboard on web because no focusable or tabIndex prop is set, making it unreachable without a mouse.
findings.proposed_fix: Add focusable={true} (React Native Web) or render as a native <button> via accessibilityRole="button" which implicitly makes it keyboard-focusable on web.

findings.description: The string ' day streak' is hardcoded English and not wrapped in a t() translation call.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with {t('streakCounter.dayStreak', { count: streakCount })} and add the key to your i18n resource files.

findings.description: Helper text including 'Longest streak:', 'Today is already counted.', and 'Log an action to extend it.' are hardcoded English strings.
findings.current_value: Longest streak: {longestStreak} days. {isFresh ? 'Today is already counted.' : 'Log an action to extend it.'}
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with t('streakCounter.longestStreak', { count: longestStreak }) and t(isFresh ? 'streakCounter.alreadyCounted' : 'streakCounter.logToExtend').

findings.description: Button label strings 'Logged for today' and 'Log today\'s progress' are hardcoded English.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with {isFresh ? t('streakCounter.loggedToday') : t('streakCounter.logProgress')}.

findings.description: The disabled visual state uses only opacity: 0.7 with no colour or label change, which is insufficient for users with low vision and fails WCAG 1.4.3 non-text contrast guidance.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the disabled style to use a distinct background colour (e.g. #6B7280) and update the text colour to ensure 4.5:1 contrast, rather than relying solely on opacity.

findings.description: An inline style array [styles.logButton, isFresh && styles.logButtonDisabled] creates a new array reference on every render, causing unnecessary reconciliation.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the computed style with useMemo: const logButtonStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.logButton, isFresh && styles.logButtonDisabled], [isFresh]);

findings.description: The inline style object { width: `${Math.max(progressPercentage, 6)}%` } creates a new object on every render even when progressPercentage has not changed.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize with useMemo: const progressFillStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.progressFill, { width: `${Math.max(progressPercentage, 6)}%` }], [progressPercentage]);

findings.description: The accessibilityLabel for the progressbar uses the variable label which may be vague or user-supplied without a guaranteed descriptive suffix.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure the label always forms a self-explanatory string, e.g. accessibilityLabel={`${label} streak: ${progressPercentage}% toward next milestone`} (≤80 chars when label is short).

findings.description: The overlay Pressable used to dismiss the modal has a vague accessibilityLabel that gives no role or action context and is missing accessibilityRole and accessibilityHint.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button" and accessibilityHint="Double-tap to dismiss" and change label to "Dismiss language selector".

findings.description: Language row items use accessibilityRole="radio" but there is no wrapping radiogroup role, which makes the radio semantics invalid for both screen readers and assistive tech.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the FlatList in a View with accessibilityRole="radiogroup" and accessibilityLabel={locale.language.selectorLabel} so the radio items have valid group context.

findings.description: The checkmark (✓) is rendered as visible text but has no accessibilityElementsHidden, so screen readers will announce it redundantly since accessibilityState.checked already conveys selection.
findings.proposed_fix: Add importantForAccessibility="no" (Android) and accessibilityElementsHidden={true} (iOS) to the checkmark ThemedText, or render it as an aria-hidden element on web.

findings.description: Flag emoji in triggerText and lang rows are exposed to screen readers without an accessibilityLabel, causing TalkBack/VoiceOver to spell out the emoji description rather than the language name.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the flag emoji in a View/Text with accessibilityElementsHidden={true} and importantForAccessibility="no" so only the language code or label is announced.

findings.description: On web, the overlay backdrop Pressable is not reachable or dismissible via Escape key; there is no onKeyDown handler for keyboard users.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a web-specific onKeyDown handler: if (e.key === 'Escape') setOpen(false), using Platform.OS === 'web' guard or a role="dialog" with proper focus trapping.

findings.description: The Modal does not trap focus on web; keyboard users can Tab behind the overlay to the underlying page content.
findings.proposed_fix: On web, implement a focus trap: auto-focus the first language row when the modal opens and intercept Tab/Shift+Tab to cycle focus within the sheet. Use a ref on the first item and call .focus() in a useEffect keyed on `open`.

findings.description: The trigger Pressable does not receive focus automatically on web when it is the primary interactive control on-screen, and lacks role="combobox" or role="button" ARIA semantics needed for web keyboard navigation.
findings.proposed_fix: On web, add aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded={open} to the trigger Pressable so keyboard and AT users understand the control's purpose and state.

findings.description: ItemSeparatorComponent is declared as an inline arrow function returning JSX, causing a new function reference and component instance on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to a stable named component outside the render tree: const Separator = () => <View style={styles.separator} />; then pass ItemSeparatorComponent={Separator}.

findings.description: The renderItem function is defined as an inline arrow function inside JSX, creating a new reference on every render and defeating FlatList's cell recycling optimisation.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract renderItem to a useCallback outside the FlatList JSX: const renderLangItem = useCallback(({ item }) => { ... }, [currentLang, handleSelect, locale]);

findings.description: onPress={() => setOpen(true)} on the trigger is an inline anonymous function creating a new reference each render.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize with useCallback: const openSelector = useCallback(() => setOpen(true), []); then pass onPress={openSelector}.

findings.description: The overlay Pressable accessibilityLabel is a hardcoded English string not sourced from the locale translations object.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with accessibilityLabel={locale.language.closeSelectorA11y} and add the corresponding key to all locale files.

findings.description: The FlatList has no ListEmptyComponent, so if LANG_CODES is ever empty the sheet renders a blank panel with no feedback to the user.
findings.proposed_fix: Add ListEmptyComponent={<ThemedText style={styles.emptyText}>{locale.language.noLanguagesAvailable}</ThemedText>} to the FlatList.

findings.description: The trigger Pressable has borderRadius: 8 while each language row has borderRadius: 10, creating inconsistent border-radius values across sibling interactive elements in the same component.
findings.proposed_fix: Align to a single token, e.g. both use borderRadius: 8 or introduce a design-token constant (e.g. radius.md = 8) applied consistently to all Pressables in this component.

findings.description: The availability-submit Pressable has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityHint, making it completely opaque to assistive technology.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button", accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.availability.addButtonA11y')}, accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.availability.addButtonHint')} to the Pressable.

findings.description: The dismiss Pressable inside the success banner has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityHint; screen-reader users only hear the raw text 'dismiss' with no context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="button", accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.availability.dismissBannerA11y')} (e.g. 'Dismiss availability saved confirmation'), accessibilityHint to the Pressable.

findings.description: The availability workerId InputField has no accessibilityLabel or accessibilityHint, so screen readers cannot describe the field's purpose.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.availability.workerIdA11y')} and accessibilityHint={t('scheduler.availability.workerIdA11yHint')} to the InputField.

findings.description: The day, from, and to InputFields inside the availability inline-inputs group all lack accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint props to each of the three InputFields, analogous to the worker-form fields above.

findings.description: Worker-form InputFields have no returnKeyType or onSubmitEditing chaining, so the keyboard 'next' action does not advance focus to the next field.
findings.current_value: Three consecutive InputFields (name, role, skills) with no returnKeyType or onSubmitEditing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add returnKeyType="next" and onSubmitEditing to each field to chain focus (name→role→role→skills→skills fires handleAddWorker); add returnKeyType="done" on the last field.

findings.description: Availability-form InputFields have no returnKeyType or onSubmitEditing chaining across workerId, day, from, and to.
findings.current_value: Four consecutive InputFields with no returnKeyType or onSubmitEditing.
findings.proposed_fix: Chain focus workerId→day→from→to with returnKeyType="next"/onSubmitEditing; set returnKeyType="done" on 'to' field to trigger handleAvailabilitySubmit.

findings.description: No autoFocus on the first InputField of the add-worker form, requiring extra tab stops on web before the user can begin typing.
findings.proposed_fix: Add autoFocus={true} (or autoFocus prop forwarding) to the name InputField so focus lands there when the section is scrolled into view or the card mounts.

findings.description: The 'Assign Now' CTA uses a combined style array [styles.secondaryButton, styles.tightButton] while the two sibling submit buttons use a single styles.primaryButton, creating visual and semantic inconsistency for equivalent CTAs.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide on one style token per role (primary vs secondary) and apply it consistently; if this button is primary, use styles.primaryButton; document the distinction in the style guide.

findings.description: None of the three Pressable buttons visually distinguish a disabled state; when the form is empty/invalid the button still looks active.
findings.current_value: style={styles.primaryButton} with no disabled prop or conditional style.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept a derived disabled boolean (e.g. workerForm.name === ''), pass disabled={isDisabled} and style={[styles.primaryButton, isDisabled && styles.primaryButtonDisabled]} to each submit Pressable.

findings.description: The 'Assign Now' Pressable uses an inline arrow function that creates a new function reference on every render, preventing memoisation of child components.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to a useCallback: const handleAssignNow = useCallback(() => { scrollToShiftSection(); setAvailabilitySuccessPromptVisible(false); router.setParams({ section: 'shifts' }); }, [scrollToShiftSection, setAvailabilitySuccessPromptVisible, router]);

findings.description: The dismiss Pressable's onPress is an inline arrow function recreated every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to useCallback: const handleDismissBanner = useCallback(() => setAvailabilitySuccessPromptVisible(false), [setAvailabilitySuccessPromptVisible]);

findings.description: The ghost-preview array [0, 1] is created as a new literal on every render inside the JSX, causing unnecessary allocation.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a module-level constant: const GHOST_INDICES = [0, 1]; and reference it in the map call.

findings.description: Worker skill tags are purely decorative Views with no accessibilityRole or accessible grouping; screen readers announce them as unlabelled.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="text" (or wrap in an accessibilityLabel combining all skills on the parent row) so VoiceOver/TalkBack reads skill badges in context.

findings.description: The ghost-container comment '/* Ghost preview — shows what populated workers look like */' is a developer comment, not user-visible, so no i18n gap, but the accessibilityElementsHidden attribute does not also set importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" for Android parity.
findings.proposed_fix: Add importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" alongside accessibilityElementsHidden to ensure the ghost container is hidden on Android as well.

findings.description: accessibilityLabel for the step Pressable is identical whether the step is complete or not because the ternary appends an empty string in both branches, so screen readers never announce completion state.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a meaningful conditional: `step.completed ? t('scheduler.onboarding.stepCompletedA11y', { step: step.title }) : t('scheduler.onboarding.stepIncompleteA11y', { step: step.title })`

findings.description: Each step Pressable is missing an accessibilityHint describing what will happen when activated.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `accessibilityHint={step.completed ? t('scheduler.onboarding.stepDoneHint') : t('scheduler.onboarding.stepActionHint', { action: step.actionLabel })}` to every Pressable.

findings.description: Progress bar View has no accessibility role or live label, so screen readers cannot announce the current onboarding progress percentage.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `accessibilityRole="progressbar"`, `accessibilityValue={{ min: 0, max: 100, now: Math.round(progress * 100) }}`, and `accessibilityLabel={t('scheduler.onboarding.progressA11y', { pct: Math.round(progress * 100) })}` to the outer progress track View.

findings.description: When step.onPress is undefined the Pressable is still rendered as an interactive button, misleading assistive technology and keyboard users.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `accessibilityState={{ disabled: !step.onPress }}` and conditionally omit `accessibilityRole="button"` or replace with `role="none"` when onPress is falsy.

findings.description: Pressable components are not guaranteed to be focusable via keyboard on web (Expo web); no tabIndex or focusable prop is set.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `focusable={true}` (React Native Web) or wrap with a web-specific `role="button"` and `tabIndex={0}` via Platform.select to ensure keyboard reachability.

findings.description: The accessibilityLabel key 'scheduler.onboarding.completedA11y' is ambiguous — it does not clearly distinguish between completed and incomplete states.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename to 'scheduler.onboarding.stepCompletedA11y' / 'scheduler.onboarding.stepIncompleteA11y' with values like "Step complete: {{step}}" and "Start step: {{step}}" (each ≤ 80 chars).

findings.description: Inner flex View uses an inline object literal style `{ flex: 1, marginHorizontal: 10 }` while all sibling layout styles use the StyleSheet — inconsistent pattern.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to `StyleSheet.create({ stepContent: { flex: 1, marginHorizontal: 10 } })` in scheduler.styles and reference as `styles.stepContent`.

findings.description: Completed steps have no visual distinction (e.g., reduced opacity, different background) compared to incomplete steps, so disabled/done states are not visually differentiated.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `step.completed && styles.onboardingStepDone` to the style array and define a muted/completed variant in the StyleSheet (e.g., reduced opacity or tick background tint).

findings.description: If `steps` is an empty array, the card renders with a title and progress bar but no items and no empty-state message, leaving a visually broken UI.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a guard: `{steps.length === 0 ? <ThemedText style={styles.mutedText}>{t('scheduler.onboarding.noSteps')}</ThemedText> : steps.map(...)}`

findings.description: A new object literal `{ flex: 1, marginHorizontal: 10 }` is created on every render for each mapped step, causing unnecessary reconciliation work.
findings.proposed_fix: Move to StyleSheet.create as described in CHK-007 so the reference is stable across renders.

findings.description: `Math.max(progress * 100, 6)` is computed inline in the JSX style prop, producing a new style object on every render.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive `const fillWidth = `${Math.max(progress * 100, 6)}%`` outside JSX (or useMemo) and reference as `{ width: fillWidth }` so the computation is not repeated per-render pass.

findings.description: The step indicator text for incomplete steps renders the raw numeric index + 1 directly without going through the translation layer, which may break in RTL or locale-specific numeral systems.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `{step.completed ? t('scheduler.onboarding.stepDoneIcon') : t('scheduler.onboarding.stepNumber', { n: index + 1 })}` to allow locale-aware numeral formatting.

findings.description: The alert container has no accessibilityHint, so screen-reader users receive no guidance on what actions are available inside the live region.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityHint="Two buttons below let you dismiss or start a 3-minute reset" to the ThemedView.

findings.description: The 'Dismiss' Pressable is missing an accessibilityHint, leaving screen-reader users without context about the consequence of the action.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityHint="Closes the wellness prompt without taking a break" to the dismiss Pressable.

findings.description: The 'Take a break' Pressable is missing an accessibilityHint, so users don't know what will happen when they activate it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityHint="Starts a guided 3-minute break session" to the primary Pressable.

findings.description: Neither Pressable sets tabIndex or accessible focus order hints, and on web there is no guarantee keyboard Tab order matches the intended dismiss-first, confirm-second flow.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tabIndex={0} (or focusable={true} for RN) to both Pressables and verify DOM order matches visual order; consider wrapping in a FocusTrap on web when the prompt is modal-like.

findings.description: The two sibling buttons have inconsistent border radii: the shared 'button' style uses borderRadius 10, while the wrapper card uses borderRadius 14, creating a visual mismatch that differs from common pill-inside-card patterns.
findings.proposed_fix: Align button borderRadius to 8 (squarer, clearly nested) or 20 (pill), and document the design token so both values derive from the same constant, e.g. const CARD_RADIUS = 14; button: { borderRadius: CARD_RADIUS - 4 }.

findings.description: Neither button has a visually distinct disabled state; if onDismiss or onTakeBreak are undefined or the parent disables interaction, there is no opacity or color change to communicate unavailability.
findings.proposed_fix: Add disabled prop support: accept optional isLoading/disabled flags in props, then set disabled={disabled} and style={[..., disabled && styles.buttonDisabled]} with styles.buttonDisabled: { opacity: 0.4 }.

findings.description: The subtitle string 'Time for a mindful pause' is a hardcoded English literal not wrapped in a translation call.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with {t('wellness.prompt.title')} and add the key to the translation files.

findings.description: The body copy including the pluralised 'minute/minutes' label is hardcoded English and not using an i18n pluralisation helper.
findings.current_value: You have been focused for {roundedMinutes} minute{roundedMinutes === 1 ? '' : 's'}.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with {t('wellness.prompt.body', { count: roundedMinutes })} and use i18next plural forms or equivalent in the translation file.

findings.description: Button labels 'Not now' and 'Take a 3-minute reset' are hardcoded English strings.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with {t('wellness.prompt.dismiss')} and {t('wellness.prompt.confirm')} respectively.

findings.description: Platform.OS === 'ios' is evaluated inside StyleSheet.create at module parse time, which is fine, but shadowOpacity uses a ternary producing a different value per platform that would be cleaner and more tree-shakeable as a Platform.select call.
findings.proposed_fix: shadowOpacity: Platform.select({ ios: 0.12, default: 0.2 })

findings.description: The pluralisation ternary inside JSX creates a new expression on every render; while trivial here, extracting it to the variable already computed (roundedMinutes) as a derived label string avoids inline branching in JSX.
findings.proposed_fix: const minuteLabel = roundedMinutes === 1 ? 'minute' : 'minutes'; then use {roundedMinutes} {minuteLabel} in JSX.

findings.description: The accessibilityLabel 'Mindful break reminder' on the alert container is slightly vague about its interactive nature; a more descriptive label improves VoiceOver announcement.
findings.proposed_fix: "Wellness check-in: you've been active for N minutes"

findings.description: accessibilityLabel concatenates title and summary which can exceed 120 chars and duplicates visible text already read by screen readers; no accessibilityHint describes the action.
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityLabel={item.title} accessibilityHint={`Relevance score ${Math.round(Math.min(1,Math.max(0,item.score))*100)}%. Tap to open.`}

findings.description: When items is empty the component returns null with no empty-state message or CTA, leaving a blank section with no user guidance.
findings.proposed_fix: if (!items.length) return (<ThemedView style={styles.container}><ThemedText>No personalized actions yet. Complete more tasks to get recommendations.</ThemedText></ThemedView>);

findings.description: The section heading 'Personalized actions' is a hardcoded English string not wrapped in a t() call.
findings.proposed_fix: <ThemedText type="subtitle">{t('personalizedFeed.heading')}</ThemedText>

findings.description: An inline arrow function is created on every render for each item's onPress, causing unnecessary re-renders for all cards when the list changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract a memoized FeedCard child component that accepts item and onSelectItem as props and calls onSelectItem(item) in a stable useCallback, preventing re-creation on every parent render.

findings.description: Math.round(Math.min(1, Math.max(0, item.score)) * 100) is recomputed inline on every render; should be derived once per item.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute const scorePercent = Math.round(Math.min(1, Math.max(0, item.score)) * 100); inside the card's render scope or within a memoized child component, then render {scorePercent}%.

findings.description: Pressable cards have no visual disabled state; if onSelectItem is undefined the card is still pressable with no feedback or aria-disabled signal.
findings.proposed_fix: Add disabled={!onSelectItem} accessibilityState={{ disabled: !onSelectItem }} and a conditional style such as [styles.card, !onSelectItem && styles.cardDisabled] with reduced opacity.

findings.description: Pressable has no pressed-state visual feedback (no style function variant or android_ripple), making it indistinguishable from a static card on press.
findings.proposed_fix: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.card, pressed && styles.cardPressed]} and add styles.cardPressed: { opacity: 0.7 } to StyleSheet, or add android_ripple={{ color: '#E5E7EB' }}.

findings.description: On web, Pressable does not receive keyboard focus or trigger onPress via Enter/Space without explicit role and tabIndex, making feed items unreachable by keyboard-only users.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tabIndex={0} and onKeyDown handler (for web) that calls onSelectItem?.(item) when event.key is 'Enter' or ' ', or wrap in a focusable component that handles both.

findings.description: The percentage badge has no accessible label explaining what the score means; screen readers will announce a bare number with no context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityLabel={`Relevance: ${scorePercent}%`} to the badge ThemedText so screen readers convey meaning.

findings.description: The '%' suffix and the implicit 'Relevance score' concept are hardcoded; unit formatting should use Intl.NumberFormat or a t() call for locale-aware percentage rendering.
findings.proposed_fix: {new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(item.score)}

findings.description: container and card both use borderRadius: 12 and gap: 10/6 defined as magic numbers; extracting to named tokens would ensure consistency if values change.
findings.proposed_fix: Define spacing and radius constants (e.g. CARD_RADIUS = 12, SPACING_MD = 10) in a shared theme file and reference them in StyleSheet to keep siblings consistent.

findings.description: Trial banner is a static View but conveys status information with no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, making it invisible to screen readers as a meaningful region.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="status" and accessibilityLabel="Pro trial active — unlimited auto-assigns enabled. $12/mo flat after trial." to the outer View so VoiceOver/TalkBack announces it as a live status region.

findings.description: The free-plan Pressable accessibilityLabel is static ('Upgrade to Pro plan') and does not reflect the dynamic state (limit reached vs. uses remaining), losing critical context for screen-reader users.
findings.proposed_fix: Set accessibilityLabel dynamically: accessibilityLabel={limitReached ? 'Upgrade to Pro — free auto-assign limit reached' : `Upgrade to Pro — ${autoAssignUsesLeft} free auto-assign${autoAssignUsesLeft === 1 ? '' : 's'} remaining`}

findings.description: accessibilityHint describes navigation ('Opens billing page') but omits the consequence of the action; hint should describe outcome not mechanism.
findings.current_value: accessibilityHint="Opens billing page to start your free Pro trial"
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityHint="Starts your 10-day free Pro trial with no per-employee fees"

findings.description: All user-visible strings (headline, CTA, pricing note, badge labels, trial copy) are hardcoded English literals with no t() internationalisation wrapper.
findings.current_value: 'Stop building rosters by hand — you\'ve hit the free limit.' / 'TRIAL' / 'FREE' / '$12/mo flat after trial...'
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap every visible string in a t() call, e.g. t('upgradeBanner.limitReachedHeadline'), and extract all literals to a locale file. Apply consistently across outcomeHeadline, outcomeCta, badge text, trial text, trialSub, and pricingNote.

findings.description: outcomeCta string 'Auto-assign your whole team in one tap. Try Pro free 10 days →' exceeds 80 chars (53 chars OK) but the limit-reached variant 'Unlock unlimited auto-assigns — no per-employee fees →' is fine; the non-limit CTA should be trimmed for clarity.
findings.current_value: 'Auto-assign your whole team in one tap. Try Pro free 10 days →'
findings.proposed_fix: 'Try Pro free — auto-assign your whole team in one tap →'

findings.description: openBilling is recreated on every render because it is defined as an inline arrow function inside the component body without useCallback, and it closes over plan which changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap with useCallback: const openBilling = useCallback(() => { void trackEvent('upgrade_cta_tapped', { plan, source: 'banner' }); Linking.openURL(CLERK_BILLING_URL).catch(() => {}); }, [plan]);

findings.description: The Pressable style prop uses an inline arrow function that constructs a new array on every render and on every press-state change, causing unnecessary re-renders of child components.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to a stable style via useMemo or accept the pressed-array pattern but memoize the base array: const baseStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.banner, styles.freeBanner], []); then style={({ pressed }) => pressed ? [...baseStyle, styles.bannerPressed] : baseStyle}

findings.description: The trial banner is a plain View while the free-plan banner is a Pressable, creating inconsistent interaction affordance — the trial banner has no tap target to manage the subscription, leaving trial users without an equivalent action.
findings.proposed_fix: Convert the trial banner to a Pressable with the same openBilling handler, accessibilityRole="button", and an appropriate accessibilityLabel such as 'Manage Pro trial — view billing details' so both banners offer a consistent interaction model.

findings.description: When plan === 'user_subscription' and isTrialing is false the component returns null silently; there is no fallback for an unknown/unrecognised plan value, which could cause the banner to vanish without explanation.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit guard for unexpected plan values: if (!plan) return null; and consider logging an error or rendering a neutral fallback for unrecognised plan strings to aid debugging.

findings.description: On Expo web, Pressable does not automatically receive a keyboard-accessible role; there is no onKeyDown handler to trigger openBilling on Enter/Space, making the banner unreachable for keyboard-only web users.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a web-specific onKeyDown prop: onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') openBilling(); }} or wrap in a native <button> element via Platform.select for web to inherit built-in keyboard support.

findings.description: No accessibilityRole is enforced, so screen readers may not announce this as a link, and callers can accidentally omit it.
findings.proposed_fix: Spread rest after setting a default: <Link accessibilityRole="link" {...rest} href={href} onPress={...} /> — this ensures a sensible default while still allowing callers to override.

findings.description: No accessibilityHint is provided to warn users that the link opens outside the app (in-app browser on native, new tab on web).
