findings.proposed_fix: Add a default hint: accessibilityHint={rest.accessibilityHint ?? 'Opens in an external browser'} as a prop on the Link element.

findings.description: target="_blank" has no rel equivalent to protect against reverse tabnapping; on web this is a security and user-trust concern.
findings.proposed_fix: Add rel="noopener noreferrer" via the Link's web-specific props or pass it through rest: <Link target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" {...rest} href={href} onPress={...} />

findings.description: The onPress handler uses event.preventDefault() but does not handle the keyboard Enter/Space activation path on web; keyboard users activating the link via keyboard events bypass onPress on some expo-router versions, potentially opening the default browser instead of the in-app browser on web-targeted builds.
findings.proposed_fix: Also wire an onKeyDown (or use the href prop guard) to ensure consistent behaviour: confirm that expo-router's Link correctly routes keyboard activation through onPress, and add an integration test for keyboard Enter key activation.

findings.description: An inline async arrow function is created on every render as the onPress prop, causing unnecessary re-renders for any memoised children that receive this component as a prop.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap with useCallback: const handlePress = useCallback(async (event) => { if (Platform.OS !== 'web') { event.preventDefault(); await openBrowserAsync(href); } }, [href]); then pass onPress={handlePress}.

findings.description: The proposed default accessibilityHint 'Opens in an external browser' is a hardcoded English string; if i18n is added later this will be missed.
findings.proposed_fix: Source the string from your i18n system: accessibilityHint={rest.accessibilityHint ?? t('externalLink.hint', 'Opens in an external browser')} so it is translatable from the start.

findings.description: TextInput is missing accessibilityRole; React Native does not automatically assign 'none' or 'text' role to TextInput on all platforms, leaving screen readers without explicit semantic context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="none" (or use role="textbox" on web via aria-role) — for React Native set accessibilityRole to a supported value; for TextInput the standard is to leave role implicit but explicitly add role='search'/'text' via the accessible prop set to true: `accessible={true} accessibilityRole="none"`. More practically, ensure `accessible={true}` is explicit so the field is always exposed as a focusable accessible element.

findings.description: accessibilityHint is entirely optional and can be undefined, meaning callers that omit it leave screen-reader users without any action guidance on what the field expects.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive a sensible default hint from the label when none is provided, e.g.: `accessibilityHint={accessibilityHint ?? `Enter ${label.toLowerCase()}`}`

findings.description: No returnKeyType prop is accepted or forwarded, so the keyboard Return key defaults to 'default' on all instances regardless of context (e.g., last field in a form should show 'done', numeric fields 'next').
findings.proposed_fix: Add `returnKeyType?: ReturnKeyTypeOptions` to the Props type and forward it to TextInput: `returnKeyType={returnKeyType ?? 'done'}`

findings.description: No onSubmitEditing prop is exposed, preventing parent forms from chaining focus to the next input field when the user presses Return/Next on the keyboard.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `onSubmitEditing?: () => void` to Props and forward it: `onSubmitEditing={onSubmitEditing}` on TextInput, then pass a ref-advancing handler from the parent form.

findings.description: No ref is forwarded from this component, making it impossible for parent forms to programmatically focus this field (e.g., autoFocus on mount or focus-chaining via onSubmitEditing).
findings.proposed_fix: Convert to forwardRef: `export const InputField = React.forwardRef<TextInput, Props>(({ ... }, ref) => ( <TextInput ref={ref} ... /> ))` so callers can call `inputRef.current?.focus()`.

findings.description: The hardcoded hex colour string '#9CA3AF' for placeholderTextColor is not a gap in itself, but the placeholder prop value passed by callers will be a hardcoded English string with no i18n wrapper enforced at this layer.
findings.proposed_fix: Document in the Props type that `placeholder` and `label` must be pre-translated by the caller (e.g., via t()), or accept a translation function and apply it internally to enforce i18n at the component boundary.

findings.description: The component is a plain arrow function with no memoisation; if the parent re-renders frequently (e.g., on every keystroke in a sibling field) this component will re-render unnecessarily even when its own props are unchanged.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap with React.memo: `export const InputField = React.memo(({ ... }: Props) => ( ... ))` to bail out of re-renders when props are referentially equal.

findings.description: The ThemedView root container has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, so screen readers announce it as a generic unlabelled region.
findings.proposed_fix: <ThemedView style={styles.lossSummary} accessibilityRole="summary" accessibilityLabel="Lost revenue summary">

findings.description: The progress bar View has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityValue, making it completely opaque to assistive technology.
findings.proposed_fix:
<View
  style={styles.progressTrack}
  accessibilityRole="progressbar"
  accessibilityLabel="Schedule improvement"
  accessibilityValue={{ min: 0, max: 100, now: Math.min(100, Math.max(0, metrics.improvement * 100)), text: improvementPercent }}
>
  <View style={[styles.progressFill, { width: improvementPercent as `${number}%` }]} />
</View>

findings.description: The delta badge View has no accessibilityLabel; screen readers will read raw symbol-prefixed currency text without context (e.g. "-$200" with no explanation).
findings.proposed_fix:
<View
  style={[styles.badge, metrics.delta >= 0 ? styles.positiveBadge : styles.badge]}
  accessibilityLabel={metrics.delta >= 0 ? `Revenue risk reduced by ${formatCurrency(metrics.delta)}` : `Revenue risk increased by ${formatCurrency(Math.abs(metrics.delta))}`}
>

findings.description: The negative delta falls back to styles.badge instead of a dedicated styles.negativeBadge, so the badge is visually identical for both positive and negative deltas — disabled/negative state is not visually distinguished.
findings.proposed_fix: metrics.delta >= 0 ? styles.positiveBadge : styles.negativeBadge  // define styles.negativeBadge in scheduler.styles.ts with a distinct background/text colour

findings.description: "Lost revenue exposure" is a hardcoded English string not wrapped in a t() translation call.
findings.proposed_fix: {t('scheduler.lostRevenueSummary.title')}

findings.description: The subtitle description string is hardcoded English and not wrapped in t().
findings.current_value: Estimated revenue at risk from uncovered roles before vs. after forecasting.
findings.proposed_fix: {t('scheduler.lostRevenueSummary.subtitle')}

findings.description: "Before forecast", "After forecast", and "Uncovered:" label strings are hardcoded English.
findings.proposed_fix: {t('scheduler.lostRevenueSummary.beforeForecast')} / {t('scheduler.lostRevenueSummary.afterForecast')} / {t('scheduler.lostRevenueSummary.uncovered', { count: metrics.baselineGap })}

findings.description: Inline style object literal `{ alignItems: 'flex-end' }` is recreated on every render, causing unnecessary re-layout work on the native side.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `afterColumn: { alignItems: 'flex-end' }` to scheduler.styles.ts and reference it as `style={styles.afterColumn}`.

findings.description: The subtitle acting as an inline tooltip/description is 82 characters and slightly exceeds the 80-char guideline; it can be tightened.
findings.current_value: Estimated revenue at risk from uncovered roles before vs. after forecasting.
findings.proposed_fix: Revenue at risk from uncovered roles, before and after forecast.

findings.description: The '+not-found' Stack.Screen has no accessibilityLabel or title option, so screen-readers will announce a raw route string to users landing on the 404 screen.
findings.proposed_fix: <Stack.Screen name="+not-found" options={{ title: 'Page Not Found', headerShown: true }} />

findings.description: The 'inner' JSX tree is reconstructed as a new object literal on every render of RootLayout, causing unnecessary re-renders of LocaleProvider and ThemeProvider subtrees.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract 'inner' into a memoised component (e.g. `const AppShell = React.memo(function AppShell() { return <LocaleProvider>...</LocaleProvider>; })`) and render <AppShell /> in both branches.

findings.description: The ThemeProvider 'value' prop receives a new object reference on every render because the ternary is evaluated inline, forcing all theme consumers to re-render even when colorScheme has not changed.
findings.proposed_fix: const theme = useMemo(() => colorScheme === 'dark' ? DarkTheme : DefaultTheme, [colorScheme]); // then: value={theme}

findings.description: useFonts is called unconditionally but the font object literal `{ SpaceMono: require(...) }` is a new reference on every render, potentially causing the hook to restart font loading.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist the fonts map outside the component: `const FONTS = { SpaceMono: require('../assets/fonts/SpaceMono-Regular.ttf') };` then call `useFonts(FONTS)`.

findings.description: The hardcoded string value for the not-found screen title (if added) and any future options.title strings in AppNavigator should be wrapped in a t() call to support localisation.
findings.proposed_fix: import { useTranslation } from your LocaleContext and use options={{ title: t('nav.notFound') }} with a corresponding locale key.

findings.description: StatusBar is placed inside ThemeProvider but outside ErrorBoundary; if the error boundary triggers, the StatusBar style may become inconsistent with the fallback UI's colour scheme.
findings.proposed_fix: Move <StatusBar style="auto" /> inside <ErrorBoundary> (after <AppNavigator />) so its style is always co-located with the rendered UI tree.

findings.description: The fallback empty string for publishableKey (`?? ''`) is a silent failure; any error message surfaced to users from auth failures will be in hardcoded English with no i18n wrapper.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure any user-visible auth error strings thrown or displayed downstream are passed through t() and that a locale key such as 'auth.missingKey' is defined in all locale files.

findings.description: accessibilityLabel 'Loading' is vague and provides no context about what content is loading.
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityLabel="Loading content, please wait"

findings.description: accessibilityRole 'progressbar' should be accompanied by accessibilityValue (min/max/now) to convey indeterminate state to screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: accessibilityRole="progressbar" accessibilityValue={{ min: 0, max: 1, now: undefined, text: 'indeterminate' }}

findings.description: The skeleton card is not marked as aria-busy, so assistive technologies on web will not know the region is in a loading state.
findings.proposed_fix: Add aria-busy={true} (or accessibilityState={{ busy: true }}) to the outer View so screen readers announce the busy state.

findings.description: Individual Animated.View skeleton rows have no accessibilityElementsHidden/importantForAccessibility set, causing screen readers to iterate over meaningless decorative rows.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityElementsHidden={true} importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" aria-hidden={true} to each Animated.View row so assistive tech skips decorative placeholders.

findings.description: Array.from({ length: rows }) is called on every render, producing a new array each time; rows is stable but the allocation is unnecessary.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the array outside render or use useMemo: const rowIndices = useMemo(() => Array.from({ length: rows }, (_, i) => i), [rows]); then map over rowIndices.

findings.description: The style array [styles.row, { opacity }] creates a new inline object literal on every render; the animated opacity value should be referenced directly via the Animated.Value ref.
findings.proposed_fix: Pre-compose the animated style outside JSX: const animatedRowStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.row, { opacity }], [opacity]); then use style={animatedRowStyle}. Because opacity is an Animated.Value ref this is safe to memoize once.

findings.description: The hardcoded English string 'Loading' (and any future user-visible label) is not wrapped in a localisation call, which will break i18n support.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap with your i18n helper: accessibilityLabel={t('skeleton.loadingLabel')} and define skeleton.loadingLabel = 'Loading content, please wait' in translation files.

findings.description: ThemedView container has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, so screen readers announce it as an opaque view with no semantic meaning when the error state is shown.
findings.proposed_fix: <ThemedView testID="error-boundary-fallback" accessibilityRole="alert" accessibilityLabel="An error occurred. Please try again." style={styles.container}>

findings.description: The error message text is rendered from error.message which may be a raw JS error string (e.g. 'undefined is not an object'); there is no accessibilityLabel to provide a sanitised, user-friendly announcement to assistive technology.
findings.proposed_fix: <ThemedText testID="error-boundary-message" accessibilityLabel={`Error detail: ${error.message}`} style={styles.message}>{error.message}</ThemedText>

findings.description: The heading 'Something went wrong', error message, button label 'Try again', accessibilityLabel 'Retry', and accessibilityHint are all hardcoded English strings not passed through a localisation function.
findings.current_value: "Something went wrong", "Try again", "Retry", "Attempt to reload the section that failed"
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap every user-visible string with t(): t('errorBoundary.title'), t('errorBoundary.retry'), t('errorBoundary.retryHint'), etc., and move them to the appropriate translation file.

findings.description: The retry Pressable has no disabled state and no visual feedback style; if onRetry is undefined the button still renders and pressing it is a no-op with no indication to the user.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a disabled prop and a pressed/disabled visual variant: disabled={!onRetry} style={({ pressed }) => [styles.button, pressed && styles.buttonPressed, !onRetry && styles.buttonDisabled]} and define buttonPressed/buttonDisabled in StyleSheet.

findings.description: Pressable uses only a static StyleSheet object for its style prop, giving no pressed feedback (opacity/background change) on any platform.
findings.proposed_fix: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.button, pressed && { opacity: 0.75 }]}

findings.description: On Expo web, Pressable does not automatically receive a keyboard-focusable role; the retry button may be unreachable via Tab key without explicit focusable or role='button' handling.
findings.proposed_fix: Add role="button" and tabIndex={0} for web, or replace with a TouchableOpacity/Button wrapped in a Platform.select to ensure native focus management on web: <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" {...(Platform.OS === 'web' ? { tabIndex: 0 } : {})} ...>

findings.description: handleRetry is defined as a class arrow function, which is fine for the class component, but DefaultFallback receives it as a new function reference only when the class instance is created; however if ErrorBoundaryInner ever re-renders without error the reference is stable — low risk but worth documenting.
findings.proposed_fix: No change required for the class pattern; if refactored to a functional component, wrap with useCallback(() => { resetState(); onRetry?.(); }, [onRetry]).

findings.description: The message text colour (#475569) is hardcoded as a hex literal in the StyleSheet; in dark mode this slate-600 colour may fail contrast against a dark ThemedView background.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a theme-aware colour token from ThemedText/useThemeColor rather than a fixed hex value, e.g. pass type="secondary" to ThemedText and let the theme handle light/dark contrast.

findings.description: When error.message is an empty string the error detail block renders nothing meaningful; there is no fallback copy to explain the situation further.
findings.proposed_fix: {error?.message ? (<ThemedText ...>{error.message}</ThemedText>) : (<ThemedText style={styles.message}>{t('errorBoundary.unknownError')}</ThemedText>)}

findings.description: Text nodes with type='link' have no accessibilityRole='link', so screen readers cannot identify them as navigable links.
findings.proposed_fix: Spread `accessibilityRole={type === 'link' ? 'link' : undefined}` onto the <Text> element, e.g.: `<Text accessibilityRole={type === 'link' ? 'link' : undefined} style={[...]} {...rest} />`

findings.description: Text nodes with type='title' or type='subtitle' carry no accessibilityRole='header', so heading structure is invisible to assistive technologies.
findings.current_value: type === 'title' ? styles.title : undefined, type === 'subtitle' ? styles.subtitle : undefined
findings.proposed_fix: Add `accessibilityRole={type === 'title' || type === 'subtitle' ? 'header' : undefined}` to the <Text> element.

findings.description: Elements rendered with type='link' are not keyboard-focusable on web; a plain <Text> is not a tab-stop, so keyboard-only users cannot activate them.
findings.proposed_fix: When type='link', render an <Pressable accessibilityRole='link'> (or a web <a> via Platform.select) wrapping the text so it receives focus and can be activated via Enter/Space on web.

findings.description: The 'link' style hardcodes a color value (#0a7ea4) inline in the StyleSheet instead of sourcing it from the theme, breaking dark-mode consistency and contradicting the component's own theming contract.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the hardcoded color from styles.link and instead pass the themed link color through `useThemeColor` (add a 'link' token to the theme), then apply it via the dynamic `{ color }` entry in the style array when type='link'.

findings.description: The style array is constructed with up to six conditional expressions on every render; this allocates a new array and re-evaluates all conditions each render even when props are unchanged.
findings.current_value: style={[ { color }, type === 'default' ? styles.default : undefined, type === 'title' ? styles.title : undefined, ... ]}
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the type-based style once with a plain lookup object outside JSX, e.g.: `const typeStyle = styles[type];` then use `style={[{ color }, typeStyle, style]}` to minimise per-render allocations.

findings.description: A new `{ color }` object literal is created on every render inside the JSX style prop, causing unnecessary style invalidation.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the color style: `const colorStyle = useMemo(() => ({ color }), [color]);` and reference `colorStyle` in the style array.

findings.description: The 'title' style sets lineHeight equal to fontSize (both 32), which truncates descenders and reduces legibility for users with low vision or custom font scaling.
findings.proposed_fix: Set lineHeight to at least 1.2× fontSize, e.g. `lineHeight: 40`, to meet WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing guidance.

findings.description: The Animated.ScrollView has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, so screen readers cannot identify it as a scrollable region.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole="scrollbar" (or the semantic equivalent) and accessibilityLabel="Main content scroll view" to the Animated.ScrollView element.

findings.description: The parallax header Animated.View wrapping headerImage has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, leaving decorative-vs-meaningful image semantics ambiguous for screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: If the header image is decorative, add accessibilityElementsHidden={true} importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants". If meaningful, add accessibilityRole="image" and a descriptive accessibilityLabel prop passed in from the parent.

findings.description: A new object literal is created on every render for contentContainerStyle, causing unnecessary style recalculations and child re-renders.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the style outside JSX or memoize it: const contentContainerStyle = useMemo(() => ({ paddingBottom: bottom }), [bottom]); then pass contentContainerStyle={contentContainerStyle}.

findings.description: An inline array literal is passed to the style prop of Animated.View on every render, creating a new array reference each time and bypassing Reanimated's style diffing optimisation.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the static portion: const headerStaticStyle = useMemo(() => [styles.header, { backgroundColor: headerBackgroundColor[colorScheme] }], [colorScheme, headerBackgroundColor]); then pass style={[...headerStaticStyle, headerAnimatedStyle]}.

findings.description: A new inline object literal for backgroundColor is created inside the style array on every render, adding unnecessary GC pressure.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to a memoized variable: const bgStyle = useMemo(() => ({ backgroundColor: headerBackgroundColor[colorScheme] }), [colorScheme, headerBackgroundColor]);

findings.description: If an accessibilityLabel is added to the ScrollView or header (per PSV-001/PSV-002), its string value must be wrapped in a t() i18n call rather than hardcoded English.
findings.proposed_fix: Use accessibilityLabel={t('parallaxScrollView.mainContentLabel')} and accessibilityLabel={t('parallaxScrollView.headerLabel')} with corresponding locale entries.

findings.description: On web, the Animated.ScrollView does not expose keyboard scroll handling (e.g. arrow keys, Page Up/Down), reducing keyboard-only navigability.
findings.proposed_fix: On web targets, wrap or enhance with a native HTML element that has tabIndex={0} and an onKeyDown handler that maps arrow/page keys to scrollRef.current?.scrollTo calls.

findings.description: HapticTab spreads BottomTabBarButtonProps but never explicitly enforces or augments accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityHint, meaning tabs lacking those props in the navigator config will be completely unannotated for screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Destructure and provide safe fallbacks: `const { accessibilityRole = 'button', accessibilityLabel, accessibilityHint, ...rest } = props;` then pass them explicitly to PlatformPressable, and add a dev-mode warning when accessibilityLabel is absent.

findings.description: An inline arrow function is created on every render and passed as the onPressIn prop, preventing referential equality checks and causing unnecessary re-renders in PlatformPressable.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap with useCallback: `const handlePressIn = useCallback((ev) => { if (process.env.EXPO_OS === 'ios') { Haptics.impactAsync(Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light); } props.onPressIn?.(ev); }, [props.onPressIn]);` and pass `onPressIn={handlePressIn}`.

findings.description: process.env.EXPO_OS is evaluated on every press event at runtime; it is a build-time constant and should be hoisted outside the component to avoid repeated environment lookups.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist outside the component: `const IS_IOS = process.env.EXPO_OS === 'ios';` then use `if (IS_IOS) {` inside the handler.

findings.description: PlatformPressable does not have an explicit onKeyDown/onKeyPress handler for web, so Enter and Space key activation—while partially handled by the underlying element—is not guaranteed to trigger the haptic branch or the forwarded onPressIn on all web targets.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an `onKeyDown` handler for web that calls the same haptic + forwarded callback when `event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ' '`, guarded by `Platform.OS === 'web'`.

findings.description: The component provides no disabled-state visual treatment; when the tab button is disabled via BottomTabBarButtonProps, there is no opacity or color change applied at this wrapper level, leaving visual feedback entirely to the navigator theme which may be inconsistent.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract `disabled` from props and apply a style: `style={[props.style, disabled && { opacity: 0.4 }]}` so disabled tabs are visually distinguishable regardless of navigator theme.

findings.description: accessibilityHint is missing on the toggle button, leaving screen-reader users without guidance on what pressing it will do.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityHint={isOpen ? 'Collapse this section' : 'Expand this section'} to the TouchableOpacity.

findings.description: The chevron IconSymbol is a decorative icon but has no accessibilityElementsHidden/importantForAccessibility='no' set, so it may be announced redundantly by screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityElementsHidden={true} importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants' to the IconSymbol.

findings.description: On web, TouchableOpacity does not natively handle Enter/Space key activation; interactive collapsible is unreachable via keyboard without explicit onKeyDown handling.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with Pressable and add onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') setIsOpen(v => !v); }} for web keyboard support, or wrap in a role='button' with tabIndex={0} on web.

findings.description: The focused style applies borderWidth:2 and padding:4, which causes a layout shift (content moves) on focus because the unfocused state has no border or padding baseline.
findings.current_value: headingFocused: { borderWidth: 2, borderColor: Colors.light.tint, borderRadius: 8, padding: 4 }
findings.proposed_fix: Add a transparent border and equal padding to the base heading style (borderWidth:2, borderColor:'transparent', padding:4, borderRadius:8) so toggling focus color does not shift layout.

findings.description: headingFocused hardcodes Colors.light.tint as borderColor in the StyleSheet, overriding the dynamic theme-aware borderColor passed via inline style and making dark-mode focus rings incorrect.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove borderColor from headingFocused in StyleSheet; rely solely on the inline style { borderColor: Colors[theme].tint } already applied conditionally.

findings.description: An inline arrow function is created on every render and passed to onPress, preventing stable reference optimisation.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract with useCallback: const toggleOpen = useCallback(() => setIsOpen(v => !v), []); then use onPress={toggleOpen}.

findings.description: A new style array object literal and a new transform array object are created on every render for the IconSymbol style prop.
findings.proposed_fix: Hoist both rotation variants into the StyleSheet (e.g. iconOpen, iconClosed) and select with style={isOpen ? styles.iconOpen : styles.iconClosed}.

findings.description: The accessibilityHint strings (once added) and any future static UI strings should be wrapped in a t() i18n call; the component currently has no internationalisation scaffolding.
findings.proposed_fix: Import and use a translation helper, e.g. accessibilityHint={t('collapsible.hint', { action: isOpen ? 'Collapse' : 'Expand' })} so hint text is localisable.

findings.proposed_fix: Extract to StyleSheet: `cardTitleRow: { flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, flexShrink: 1 }` and reference as `style={styles.cardTitleRow}`

findings.description: Inline style object `{ flexShrink: 1 }` is recreated on every render inside the JSX prop for ThemedText.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `cardTitle: { flexShrink: 1 }` to the StyleSheet and use `style={styles.cardTitle}`

findings.description: The `children` prop is rendered unconditionally; if a consumer passes no meaningful children the card will render as an empty box with no fallback message or CTA.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept an optional `emptyMessage` prop and render it when React.Children.count(children) === 0: `{React.Children.count(children) === 0 ? <ThemedText style={styles.mutedText}>{emptyMessage ?? t('sectionCard.empty')}</ThemedText> : children}`

findings.description: The optional subtitle ThemedText has no accessibilityRole or way to associate it with the section heading, reducing context for screen-reader users.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `accessibilityRole="none"` and consider combining subtitle into the parent region's `accessibilityLabel` so it is read as part of the heading context.

findings.description: The outer View has no accessibilityRole, accessibilityLabel, or accessibilityHint, so screen readers will announce two disconnected text nodes instead of a single meaningful availability slot.
findings.proposed_fix: <View style={styles.badge} accessibilityRole="text" accessibilityLabel={`Available on ${day} from ${from} to ${to}`}>

findings.description: The muted time-range text '{from} - {to}' uses a plain hyphen-minus as a separator, which screen readers vocalise as 'dash' or skip; an en-dash or explicit aria phrasing improves comprehension.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with an accessible string: `{from}–{to}` (en-dash) and rely on the parent View's accessibilityLabel for the full reading, hiding these children with accessibilityElementsHidden / importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" so the composite label is read once.

findings.description: The confetti View has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, so screen readers may announce meaningless decorative content on native.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `accessible={false}` and `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` (Android) / `accessibilityElementsHidden={true}` (iOS) to suppress the decorative overlay from the accessibility tree entirely.

findings.description: The rotate interpolation object `{ inputRange, outputRange }` is recreated on every render for every particle because it is defined inside the render path of the map callback.
findings.proposed_fix: Pre-compute and cache `spin` alongside the other Animated.Values inside `createParticle` (or in the `useMemo` that builds particles), so each interpolation is created once and reused across renders.

findings.description: An inline style object literal containing `backgroundColor`, `width`, and `height` is constructed on every render for every particle, defeating StyleSheet memoisation and creating unnecessary GC pressure.
findings.current_value: style={[styles.particle, { backgroundColor: particle.color, width: particle.size, height: particle.size, transform: [...] }]}
findings.proposed_fix: Store the static per-particle style (backgroundColor, width, height) as a pre-computed StyleSheet entry or plain object on the particle itself inside `createParticle`/`useMemo`, then spread only the dynamic `transform` array alongside it.

findings.description: `Math.random()` is called inside the `useEffect` body (for `fallDistance` and `scatter`) on every `running` change, producing non-deterministic, non-memoised values that cannot be tested or replicated.
findings.current_value: const fallDistance = 140 + Math.random() * 60; const scatter = particle.startX + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 40;
findings.proposed_fix: Pre-compute `fallDistance` and the random scatter offset inside `createParticle` and store them on the particle object so animation parameters are stable, deterministic per particle lifetime, and derived only once.

findings.description: Using array index as the `key` prop for a static, never-reordered list is acceptable here, but is a lint warning source; using a stable unique id would be cleaner.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an `id` field (e.g. `id: Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)`) in `createParticle` and use `key={particle.id}`.

findings.description: There are no user-visible strings in this file currently, but if an `accessibilityLabel` is added for the live-region announcement of the animation, it must be wrapped in a `t()` call.
findings.proposed_fix: When adding any future accessible description string, wrap it with the app's i18n helper, e.g. `accessibilityLabel={t('confetti.animationLabel')}`.

findings.description: Users with vestibular/motion-sensitivity preferences (prefers-reduced-motion) are not respected; the animation always runs when `running` is true.
findings.proposed_fix: Check `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` (or subscribe to the event) and bail out of starting the stagger animation when the user has requested reduced motion, matching the `disabled` guard pattern already present.

findings.description: The stagger animation is started but never explicitly stopped or reset when `running` flips back to false, potentially leaving animations in flight if the parent unmounts or `running` toggles rapidly.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture the return value of `.start()` or store the `CompositeAnimation` and call `.stop()` in the `useEffect` cleanup: `const anim = Animated.stagger(40, animations); anim.start(); return () => anim.stop();`.

findings.description: A new object literal `{ backgroundColor }` is created on every render inside the style array, causing unnecessary re-renders for any memo-ised children that receive this view as a parent.
findings.proposed_fix: Memoize the derived style: `const bgStyle = useMemo(() => ({ backgroundColor }), [backgroundColor]);` then use `style={[bgStyle, style]}`.

findings.description: `ThemedView` spreads `otherProps` onto a bare `View` but never defaults `accessibilityRole`; callers that use it as a landmark container (e.g. screen root) will have no semantic role announced to assistive technologies.
findings.proposed_fix: Document that callers must pass `accessibilityRole` when the view acts as a landmark, and add a dev-only warning: `if (__DEV__ && otherProps.accessible && !otherProps.accessibilityRole) console.warn('ThemedView: accessible={true} set without accessibilityRole');`

findings.description: No hardcoded strings are present in this file, but the component exposes no mechanism to forward `accessibilityLabel` defaults, meaning consumers may forget to localise labels when wrapping this component.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a TypeScript comment in `ThemedViewProps` reminding consumers: `/** Localise via i18n before passing. */` on the inherited `accessibilityLabel` prop to surface the requirement at the call site.
